properties.name: The confirmation ledger re-read every artifact's history once per capability, which put loop_status at 30 s on reflow2's design and over flo2.io's 30 s door
properties.statement:
Found by phase 0 of the move of reflow2's design onto flo2.io (a rehearsal on the droplet, 2026-10-09). With reflow2 0.81.0, loop_status took 46.3 s cold and 30.8 s warm there, against the gateway's 30 s limit per engine call. Locally it took 30.0 s one-shot. con:loop-status-warm-latency-ms (2,000 ms warm, accepted 2026-09-05) had no check that measures it, so the growth went unnoticed after September's fix brought it to 1.3 s.

MEASURED, section by section, release build on a copy of the store: confirmation_ledger 17.4 s; every other section of loop_status under 0.1 s together; the open 0.9 s. Counted from the export: 943,665 node reads to classify accepts (art:service alone 88,413) against 4,001 if each accepting event were classified once.

REFUTED ON THE WAY: incoming() walking the whole edge set. A comment in coherence.rs said so, from 2026-08-24. Today it is an indexed prefix scan (scan_incoming_edges over CF_ADJ_IN), and the comment is corrected.

AFTER THE FIX (each artifact's and each event's facts computed once per ledger; the answer unchanged): ledger 0.26 s; core loop_status 7.2 s cold and 0.47 s warm locally; on the droplet 11.7 s cold and 0.8 s warm, with the export working and peak memory 677 MB.

A MEASUREMENT OF MINE THAT WAS WRONG, recorded so its numbers are not reused: a second droplet run read 43.0 s and 33.3 s. It measured the FIRST run's server, which had survived because I stopped the /usr/bin/time wrapper and not the server under it. The new server could not bind the port. The empty export in that run was the tell.

THE CLASS: a per-capability rollup recomputing facts that belong to shared artifacts and events, so its cost grows as capabilities × history. Pinned by art:test-the-confirmation-ledger-reads-each-history-once, which counts the ledger's store reads, so it does not depend on the hardware.
